title: Units and associativity from normalized binary extension comparisons
statement: For every coefficient immersion $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ [def-sfb-locally-closed-module-extension-data], let $F_a:\operatorname{Mod}(S)\to\operatorname{Mod}(X)$ be the fixed fully faithful extension with restriction $r_a:a^*F_a\cong1$ [def-sfb-locally-closed-module-extension-model]. Suppose natural isomorphisms $\gamma_{a,b}:F_a\circ F_b\cong F_{ab}$ are supplied for all composable pairs, satisfying the normalization of [lem-sfb-locally-closed-module-extension-binary]: $(ab)^*(\gamma_{a,b,M});r_{ab,M}=\chi_{a,b,F_aF_bM};b^*(r_{a,F_bM});r_{b,M}$, where $\chi:(ab)^*\cong b^*a^*$ is the specified inverse-image compositor and a semicolon means first the left arrow, then the right. There exist natural identity comparisons $e_X:F_{1_X}\cong1_{\operatorname{Mod}(X)}$ such that, after transport along the canonical coefficient-immersion equalities $a1_S=a$ and $1_Xa=a$ and the functor unitors, $\gamma_{a,1_S}=F_a e_S$ and $\gamma_{1_X,a}=e_X F_a$. For all $d:W\hookrightarrow T$, $b:T\hookrightarrow S$ and $a:S\hookrightarrow X$, the supplied comparisons obey $(F_a\gamma_{b,d});\gamma_{a,bd}=(\gamma_{a,b}F_d);\gamma_{ab,d}$, after the functor associator and transport along $(ab)d=a(bd)$. This conditional assertion constructs no binary geometric comparison and asserts no open or closed boundary normalization.

proof.text: Use the open boundary comparison for the identity immersion and its actual inverse-image identity comparison to construct the normalized identity isomorphism. Canonical inverse-image unit coherence makes each unit path and gamma have the same restriction; full faithfulness of the fixed model makes them equal.

The two canonical fibre-product associativity maps have the same projections, hence are equal. Conjugation through the actual module adjunctions yields both coefficient-immersion associativity and pullComp associativity. Apply the supplied binary normalization twice along each extension path and use naturality to move the intermediate restriction maps. The inverse-image associativity equation identifies the two restrictions. The source is isomorphic to a value of the triple-composite extension by two gamma maps. Full faithfulness and modelRestriction cancel restriction and identify the two paths.
